g1|variants|dunning and collections.family_title: SAP S/4HANA OTC Dunning and Collections
g1|variants|dunning and collections.summary: This scenario family covers the processes used to monitor overdue customer open items and execute collection strategies. Variants differ based on whether classic FI dunning, integrated collections management, or automated dispute management is deployed.

variants.name: Classic Financial Accounting Dunning
variants.when_used: Standard dunning run initiated in FI-AR to generate reminder letters for overdue customer invoices without advanced debt collection worklists.
variants.key_config: Define dunning areas, dunning intervals, dunning levels, and dunning charges in transaction OBV3 / OBVW.

variants.name: SAP Collections Management (FSCM-COL)
variants.when_used: Proactive receivables management utilizing worklists, collection strategies, and contact history for key accounts.
variants.key_config: Assign customer master to collection segments, define collection strategies, and configure rule groups in FSCM Collections Management.

variants.name: Integrated Dispute Management (FSCM-DIS)
variants.when_used: Handling customer deductions, short-payments, and disputed OTC billing documents tied to collections workflows.
variants.key_config: Configure dispute case types, reason codes, process routes, and integration with SD billing and FI-AR posting.

g1|core|dunning and collections|classic.title: Classic Financial Accounting Dunning
g1|core|dunning and collections|classic.story: Imagine a giant digital reminder robot that checks customer accounts every single day to see who has not paid their bills on time. When it finds overdue items, it automatically generates polite reminders or stern warning letters based on how late the payment is. In SAP S/4HANA Order-to-Cash, this process scans open customer receivables generated from billing documents, calculates dunning levels, and prints or emails correspondence to chase late cash. This ensures our company gets paid faster and keeps cash flowing smoothly.
g1|core|dunning and collections|classic.why_business_needs_it: Automating the accounts receivable collection process ensures timely follow-up on overdue customer invoices without relying on manual ledger reviews. It reduces Days Sales Outstanding (DSO) and protects cash flow by systematically escalating payment reminders.

g1|core|dunning and collections|sap coll.title: SAP Collections Management (FSCM-COL)
g1|core|dunning and collections|sap coll.story: Just like a polite robot reminding parents to pay for school lunch so kids can keep getting hot meals, the system looks at open customer invoices and tells the accounts receivable team who to call first. Technically, SAP Financial Supply Chain Management Collections Management (FIN-FSCM-COL) synchronizes Financial Accounting [FI] customer open items into a prioritized collection worklist using a collection strategy based on rules like days in arrears and promise-to-pay status.
g1|core|dunning and collections|sap coll.why_business_needs_it: Order-to-Cash teams need automated prioritization of overdue accounts instead of manual spreadsheet reviews to reduce Days Sales Outstanding [DSO] and improve cash flow. Without it, collectors waste time calling fully paid accounts or low-risk customers while high-risk overdue balances age past terms.

g1|core|dunning and collections|integrat.title: Integrated Dispute Management (FSCM-DIS)
g1|core|dunning and collections|integrat.story: Imagine a giant cash register where customers sometimes argue about a charge on their bill instead of paying right away. In SAP S/4HANA Order-to-Cash, Financial Supply Chain Management Dispute Management (FSCM-DIS) captures these customer objections directly from billing and customer accounts, putting the disputed amount on hold so dunning runs skip it until the investigation finishes.
g1|core|dunning and collections|integrat.why_business_needs_it: Integrating dispute management into the Order-to-Cash cycle prevents collection teams from sending aggressive dunning letters for disputed invoices, protecting customer relationships while tracking financial loss root causes across billing, pricing, and logistics.

g1|panel|dunning and collections.otc_impact: Dunning and collections sit at the tail end of the Order-to-Cash value stream, converting billed accounts receivable into realized cash while protecting working capital. When customer accounts fall past terms, automated dunning runs and collections worklists block new sales orders and outbound deliveries, mitigating credit risk. Efficient collections reduce Day Sales Outstanding (DSO) and improve cash flow forecasting without degrading customer experience.

panel_qa.question: How do we balance aggressive dunning with customer retention when automated reminders block sales orders?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: We balance risk mitigation and customer retention by configuring tiered dunning procedures in Financial Accounting (FI-AR) that start with gentle customer statements before escalating to legal notices and order blocks. SAP allows dunning level assignments per line item or account level, ensuring that minor delays do not immediately disrupt critical sales fulfillment. Key configuration involves dunning areas, dunning keys, and integration with SD credit management via transaction OVA8. The leadership value is optimized working capital and reduced Days Sales Outstanding (DSO) while protecting key account relationships. Next steps involve reviewing dunning blockage rules with regional sales directors during monthly working capital reviews.
panel_qa.trap: We block all orders immediately when a single invoice is overdue by one day, regardless of customer tier.

panel_qa.question: Why deploy SAP Collections Management alongside classic FI dunning instead of relying solely on standard correspondence?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: Classic FI dunning is purely reactive and document-centric, whereas SAP Collections Management (FIN-FSCM-COL) provides a proactive, profile-driven worklist for collectors based on scoring and customer contact history. SAP is configured this way to transition accounts receivable teams from passive statement issuers to active portfolio managers using integration with FI-AR open items and Credit Management (FIN-FSCM-CR). Key configuration includes defining collector groups, assigning customer segments, and setting up valuation rules in Customizing path Financial Supply Chain Management -> Collections Management. The leadership value is improved collector productivity and lower bad debt write-offs through prioritized follow-up on high-risk accounts. Next steps include rolling out promised-to-pay tracking and automated customer contact scheduling.
panel_qa.trap: Collections management is just another reporting tool that duplicates the standard customer aging report.

panel_qa.question: How does Integrated Dispute Management handle short-paid invoices without breaking the OTC billing and cash application reconciliation?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: Integrated Dispute Management (FIN-FSCM-DIS) creates a separate dispute case directly from the billing document or cash application screen when a customer deducts or shorts payment. SAP links this dispute case to the original SD invoice and FI open item, placing a temporary payment block or dunning exclusion on the disputed amount while leaving undisputed amounts open for collection. Key configuration involves dispute case types, root cause codes, and integration settings in Financial Supply Chain Management -> Dispute Management -> Process Integration with Accounts Receivable. The leadership value is transparent deduction tracking, reduced dispute resolution cycle times, and accurate aging reports. Next steps involve training customer service teams on fast-track root cause categorization.
panel_qa.trap: We write off all customer deductions immediately to clear the aging report without investigating the root cause.

panel_qa.question: What prevents dunning runs from issuing notices for disputed or legally blocked invoices?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: Dunning runs exclude disputed items by respecting dunning keys, dunning blocks on master data, and integration links from SAP Dispute Management. SAP ensures data integrity by checking the dunning block field (BSEG-MSCHL) and the dispute case status before selecting open items in transaction F150. Key configuration includes defining dunning block reasons in Financial Accounting -> Accounts Receivable and Accounts Payable -> Business Transactions -> Dunning -> Basic Settings for Dunning. The leadership value is compliance with local credit regulations and prevention of customer friction caused by erroneous collection letters. Next steps include auditing automated dunning exclusion rules quarterly.
panel_qa.trap: Collectors manually review every single dunned invoice to ensure no active disputes are included.

panel_qa.question: How do collections and dispute metrics impact overall Order-to-Cash KPIs like DSO and Cash Conversion Cycle?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: Collections and dispute metrics directly dictate the speed at which receivables are converted into cash, directly driving down DSO and shortening the Cash Conversion Cycle. SAP connects collection effectiveness indices and average dispute resolution times directly to finance dashboards in SAP Analytics Cloud. Key configuration involves setting up aging brackets and receivables key figures in Financial Supply Chain Management reporting. The leadership value is predictable cash inflows and optimized liquidity management for treasury operations. Next steps include linking collector performance bonuses to DSO reduction targets.
panel_qa.trap: We measure OTC success purely on total sales volume booked, ignoring collections performance and overdue receivables.

panel_qa.question: What is the S/4HANA cloud roadmap impact on legacy dunning and collections custom programs?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: S/4HANA Cloud mandates standard Fiori apps and SAP Best Practices, deprecating legacy SAP GUI batch jobs and custom Z-programs for dunning and collections. SAP provides standardized Fiori apps like 'Manage Collections Worklist' and 'Process Receivables' backed by the Universal Journal (ACDOCA). Key configuration involves activating standard CDS views and Fiori analytical apps for receivables management. The leadership value is reduced total cost of ownership (TCO) and real-time visibility into cash collections across global entities. Next steps include migrating legacy custom dunning correspondence forms to Adobe Document Services.
panel_qa.trap: We will rewrite our massive custom Z-dunning batch programs to run inside the S/4HANA core exactly as they did in ECC.
